The absolute-trend gate remains active and validated for risk control; no single narrative dominates.
emerging_watch: Watch for a confirmed leadership handoff from Memory/HBM to Cybersecurity. Criterion: Cybersecurity's rank score sustains above Memory's for 5 consecutive daily observations and the durability/breadth metrics remain favorable. Kill-criterion: Memory regains the top rank with improved breadth (>0.7) and durability bar recovers above 0.65.

theses.thesis: Cybersecurity exhibits the strongest coincident trend persistence (hurst 'trend'), full breadth (1.0), and a very high durability bar (0.90) among eligible themes, which suggests the absolute-trend gate will likely keep exposure viable. Crowding (z=1.95) is a caution for position sizing, not a fade. We lean overweight under the assumption that the internal health of the trend (breadth, durability) can support continuation, but acknowledge the poor track record of cross-sectional momentum as a forward indicator.
theses.dissent: High crowding and failure of cross-sectional momentum as a predictor mean this theme could abruptly reverse if a macro shock triggers a rotation away from crowded software names; the trend may already be mature.

falsifier.text: Cybersecurity's breadth falls below 0.70 for 3 consecutive days, or its durability bar drops below 0.70.
